definitions.explanation: Being separated from someone, especially a loved one, with emotional weight. Implies a significant, often permanent separation.
The formal dissolution of a marriage or the act of husband and wife separating. A formal or literary alternative to {離婚|りこん}.

examples.japanese: {親子|おやこ}の{離別|りべつ}はつらい。
examples.english: Separation between parent and child is painful.

examples.japanese: {戦争|せんそう}で{家族|かぞく}と{離別|りべつ}した。
examples.english: I was separated from my family by the war.

examples.japanese: {幼|おさな}い{頃|ころ}に{母親|ははおや}と{離別|りべつ}し、{祖父母|そふぼ}に{育|そだ}てられた。
examples.english: Separated from my mother at a young age, I was raised by my grandparents.

examples.japanese: {夫婦|ふうふ}が{離別|りべつ}する。
{離別|りべつ}{後|ご}、{子供|こども}の{親権|しんけん}が{問題|もんだい}になった。
examples.english: After the divorce, child custody became an issue.

examples.japanese: {両親|りょうしん}が{離別|りべつ}したのは{私|わたし}が{五歳|ごさい}のときだった。
examples.english: My parents divorced when I was five years old.

notes:
Composed of {離|り} (separate, leave) + {別|べつ} (part, divide). Carries a more emotional and literary tone than everyday words for separation or divorce.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {家族|かぞく}との{離別|りべつ}: separation from family
- {夫婦|ふうふ}の{離別|りべつ}: marital separation
- {離別|りべつ}を{経験|けいけん}する: to experience separation
- {離別|りべつ}{後|ご}: after the separation/divorce

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {別離|べつり}: parting, separation — more literary and poetic; emphasizes emotional pain
- {離婚|りこん}: divorce — the standard legal and everyday term for divorce
- {離散|りさん}: dispersal, scattering — used when family members are scattered to different places, often by war or disaster
- {別|わか}れ: parting, farewell — the most common everyday word for parting

REGISTER:
Formal and somewhat literary. In everyday conversation, {別|わか}れ or {離婚|りこん} would be more natural.
